entry.description: Let two processes that spell the log path differently share one inter-process file lock. `InterProcessLock` named its mutex after the configured path before that path was resolved, so a relative and an absolute spelling of one file took two different mutexes and excluded nothing. The name comes from the resolved path now. That resolves a relative path and nothing else: symbolic links, hard links, 8.3 short names, letter case and UNC versus mapped-drive spellings still produce different names. The name is also unprefixed, which on Windows makes it per-session, so a service and an interactive process have never coordinated through it (audit da18b6fd-f031, fixed by @FreeAndNil)
